interpretation: Before handling food the robot cleans its end-effectors (or puts on fresh food-safe gloves) per food-safety protocol (soap and water with 20 s of scrubbing, then a clean towel), and does it again after any contamination source (trash, pet, phone, raw meat) before touching ready-to-eat food.
conditional: implicit: contamination event mid-prep (touched trash, pet, raw chicken) -> rewash/change gloves before next ready-to-eat contact; no such event -> single initial wash suffices.
success: End-effector contamination state is clean at the first food contact and at every ready-to-eat contact after a contamination event; each wash used soap with >= 20 s scrub; drying towel was clean.
wrong: Washes once at the start, then handles the trash or the dog and keeps cooking.
Rinses without soap, or for under 20 s.
Dries on the dish towel that wiped up raw-chicken juice.
fidelity: S: contamination-tracking state machine on end-effectors
notes: For a humanoid, 'hands' map to end-effectors or gloves; grounding is through contamination propagation into food, not the gesture.

interpretation: Fetch exactly the ingredients a recipe or request calls for from fridge, freezer, pantry and spice rack, telling look-alikes apart (baking soda vs powder, salted vs unsalted butter, sugar vs salt), checking dates and spoilage, closing fridge/freezer doors, and setting everything at the prep area.
success: Each required ingredient present at the prep area with an exact type match; none expired or spoiled; fridge/freezer doors closed; perishables not left out beyond their limit.
wrong: Grabs baking powder instead of baking soda.
Brings milk past its date or spoiled.
Leaves the fridge door ajar.
fidelity: S: ingredient identity and freshness state
user_sim: Hidden: which variant the cook means for underspecified items ('the cheese' when cheddar and parmesan are both present). Necessary question: when the recipe/context doesn't disambiguate. Unnecessary: asking where the milk is (searchable).
notes: Food-prep retrieval trio L323-L325.

interpretation: Fetch the utensils the task needs, matching them to cookware and purpose (silicone or wood spatula for nonstick, measuring spoons rather than eating spoons, whisk vs fork), carrying knives by the handle with the blade down and placing them away from the counter edge.
success: Required utensils at the prep area; all compatible with the cookware (no metal on nonstick); knives placed blade-away and not overhanging the counter edge; drawers closed.
wrong: Brings a metal spatula for a nonstick pan.
Carries a knife blade-forward, or leaves it overhanging the counter edge.
Brings an eating tablespoon instead of a measuring tablespoon.
fidelity: S: tool-task compatibility; G: knife carry orientation
notes: Food-prep retrieval trio L323-L325.

interpretation: Read a recipe from a card, cookbook page, screen or handwritten note and turn it into a correct structured plan: ingredients with quantities and units (tsp vs tbsp, metric vs imperial, fractions), equipment, temperatures, times, servings and step order, including notes in margins or a second column.
success: Robot's parsed recipe (ingredients, amounts and units, oven temperature, timings, step order) matches ground truth exactly on units and amounts; missing or ambiguous items are flagged; when asked to read it aloud, the spoken content matches.
wrong: Confuses tsp and tbsp (3x error).
Misreads a fraction ('1 1/2' as '11/2') or the oven temperature unit (F vs C).
Skips a step printed in a second column or a margin note.
fidelity: S: perception of rendered text into a recipe schema
notes: To be honest the recipe must be rendered as an image or document; giving the agent the structured recipe would turn this into a no-op.

interpretation: Carry out a recipe in order, respecting dependencies and timing (preheat before the batter is ready, cream butter and sugar before adding eggs, rest/proof times, parallel steps) and judging doneness from food state rather than blindly trusting the timer, never leaving a hot burner unattended.
success: Final dish state matches the recipe target (composition, mixing state, doneness/internal temperature); step-order constraints satisfied; oven/burner never unattended while on; appliances off at the end.
wrong: Dumps all ingredients in at once.
Skips preheating and bakes in a cold oven.
Ignores doneness and pulls the dish on the timer while it is raw in the middle.
fidelity: P: thermal doneness and mixing state over time
notes: Compound; each sub-step maps to entries L322-L340 and the cooking section.

interpretation: Measure ingredients by volume with proper technique: flour spooned in and leveled (not scooped and packed), brown sugar packed, liquids in a liquid measuring cup on a flat surface read at the meniscus, using measuring spoons and correct unit conversions.
success: Measured quantity within +/-5% of target in mass-equivalent terms (e.g. spooned flour about 125 g/cup vs scooped about 150 g); correct tool type for dry vs liquid.
wrong: Scoops flour straight from the bag, packing it (about 20% too much).
Measures liquid in a dry cup or reads the cup from above/tilted.
Uses an eating spoon instead of a measuring spoon.
fidelity: P: granular packing density vs technique; liquid meniscus
notes: Primitive 'Measure.' (L2249); tool-handling 'Measure distance' (L1433) is a different sense.

interpretation: Weigh ingredients on a digital kitchen scale: place the container, tare to zero, add to the target in the correct unit mode (g vs oz), remove any excess, and stay within the scale's capacity.
success: Net ingredient mass within +/-2% (or +/-1 g for small amounts) of target; container mass excluded (tared); unit mode correct.
wrong: Forgets to tare and includes the bowl's mass.
Reads ounces as grams.
Overshoots and doesn't remove the excess.
fidelity: S: scale state machine and mass accounting
notes: Primitive 'Weigh.' (L2250); related 'Weigh suitcase' (L1874).

interpretation: Count out discrete ingredients exactly (eggs, lemons, chicken thighs, garlic cloves), distinguishing cloves from heads and leaving out cracked or spoiled units.
success: Exact count of the correct item type at the prep area; garlic delivered as cloves when cloves are asked for; no cracked/spoiled units included.
wrong: Brings 3 heads of garlic for '3 cloves'.
Includes a cracked egg.
Miscounts by one.
fidelity: S: count and part/whole identity
notes: Primitive 'Count.' (L2248); inventory counts (L1698-L1707) are a different context.

interpretation: Pour granular or dry solids (rice, sugar, flour, cereal, lentils) from a bag or canister into a measuring cup, bowl or funnel at a controlled rate, avoiding avalanches, flour clouds and overflow, then reseal the bag.
success: Target amount within tolerance; spilled grains <= threshold; no flour cloud; source resealed.
wrong: Tips the bag too steeply so contents avalanche and overflow.
Pours flour from a height and creates a cloud.
Leaves the bag open (pantry pests).
fidelity: P: granular flow vs tilt angle (angle of repose)
notes: Pour pair with L331 (liquids); granular model reused by pet-food measuring (L940).

interpretation: Scoop ingredients with a scoop or cup from bulk containers (flour bin, ice cream, cookie-dough portioning) in consistent, level-as-required portions, using a dry scoop for dry goods and separate scoops for allergen-free containers.
conditional: implicit: frozen-hard product (ice cream) -> temper or use a warm scoop; normal -> scoop directly. Allergen-free container -> dedicated clean scoop.
success: Portion count correct and mass coefficient of variation <= 10%; no cross-contact into allergen-free container; no wet-scoop clumping.
wrong: Scoops flour with a wet scoop and leaves clumps.
Uses the same scoop for the allergen and allergen-free containers.
Produces wildly uneven portions.
fidelity: P: granular/viscous scoop fill fraction
notes: Primitive 'Scoop.' (L2275); 'Scoop litter box' (L956) is a different context.

interpretation: Spoon small amounts (sauce, yogurt, jam, spices, or flour into a measuring cup) from source to target with a measuring or serving spoon, level or heaped as specified, without drips between them and without double-dipping into shared jars.
success: Amount within +/-10% of target; no drip trail; source jar uncontaminated (spoon used for tasting never re-dipped).
wrong: Tastes and re-dips the spoon into the shared jar.
Drips sauce across the stovetop.
Uses a heaped measuring spoon when a level one is specified.
fidelity: P: viscous spoon load and dripping
notes: Transfer verbs family L331-L335.

interpretation: Move contents from one container to another (decant flour into a canister, chopped vegetables from board to pot with a bench scraper, leftovers into storage) completely and without spilling, into a destination that is food-safe and big enough, labelling stored food with name and date and keeping older stock usable first.
conditional: implicit: transfer for storage -> label with name/date and use FIFO (don't bury old stock); transfer for immediate cooking -> no label needed.
success: At least 95% of contents in the destination; spill <= threshold; destination food-safe with capacity >= volume and closed; storage containers labelled with name/date; old stock not buried under new.
wrong: Picks a container that is too small and overflows.
Uses a non-food container (a cleaned paint bucket or chemical bottle).
Leaves look-alikes unlabelled (sugar vs salt) or dumps new flour on top of old.
fidelity: P: transfer completeness and spill
notes: Related: 'Transfer food into storage containers' (L467).

interpretation: Wash fruit under cool running water without soap, rubbing firm fruit, treating berries gently, scrubbing melon rinds before cutting, and washing berries only just before they are eaten, not before they go into storage.
conditional: implicit: fruit for immediate use -> wash now; going into storage (berries) -> don't wash (moisture causes mould). Firm (apple, melon) -> rub/scrub; delicate (raspberries) -> gentle rinse in colander.
success: Surface contaminant <= threshold on fruit to be eaten; no soap residue; no bruising of delicate fruit; berries headed to storage are dry/unwashed.
wrong: Washes fruit with dish soap.
Washes berries and refrigerates them wet (mould).
Scrubs raspberries and crushes them.
fidelity: P: bruise force on soft fruit and surface moisture
notes: Produce washing pair with L337; storage vs eat-now branch randomized.

interpretation: Wash vegetables by type: separate leafy greens and soak them in a bowl so grit settles, then lift them out (not pour); split leeks; scrub root vegetables with a brush; wipe or briefly rinse mushrooms; then dry greens in a salad spinner; never use soap.
success: Grit/soil <= threshold including inside leek layers; no soap; greens dried; mushrooms not waterlogged.
wrong: Pours greens and gritty water through a colander so the grit settles back on.
Soaks mushrooms until waterlogged.
Doesn't split leeks, leaving grit inside.
fidelity: P: sediment settling and waterlogging
notes: Produce washing pair with L336.

interpretation: Peel vegetables (carrots, potatoes, cucumbers, butternut squash) thinly with a peeler or knife, stroking away from the hand and body, removing potato eyes and green patches, and sending the peels to compost or trash per the household stream.
success: Peel coverage >= 98%; flesh loss <= 10% by mass; green patches and eyes removed; peels in the correct stream; no cut events.
wrong: Peels toward the hand holding the vegetable in the blade path.
Leaves green patches on potatoes.
Peels so thickly half the vegetable is wasted.
fidelity: P: peel thickness and coverage over a curved surface
notes: Peel pair with L339; cutting skills continue in later food-prep entries.

interpretation: Peel fruit by its type: hand-peel citrus and remove pith, peel bananas, peel apples with a peeler, and use a knife on mango or pineapple (cutting away from the hand), without crushing soft fruit, and only where peeling is wanted.
conditional: implicit: preference/recipe -> apple slices for a toddler peeled vs a recipe keeping the skin; fruit type decides the tool.
success: Peel removed per fruit type (citrus pith <= threshold, apple coverage >= 98%); flesh loss minimal; no crushing; no cut events; peeling matches preference/recipe.
wrong: Crushes a soft mango or kiwi while peeling.
Cuts toward the palm on a mango.
Peels apples that the recipe/person wanted with skin on.
fidelity: P: soft-fruit deformation and peel coverage
user_sim: Hidden: whether the eater wants a fruit peeled (e.g. toddler apples peeled). Necessary question: when no recipe or known preference covers it. Unnecessary: for bananas or oranges, which are always peeled.
notes: List-2 'awkward produce (squash, pineapple, mango, coconut)' (L2465).

interpretation: Remove stems correctly for each kind of produce: strip leaves from woody herb stems (rosemary, thyme), cut kale and chard ribs, pull grape and tomato stems, hull strawberries minimally, twist out tough shiitake stems, and keep the tender cilantro stems the recipe can use.
conditional: implicit: produce type -> stems discarded (rosemary, kale ribs, shiitake) vs kept (cilantro, parsley tender stems) per recipe/household.
success: Stems removed per produce type; edible yield loss <= threshold; leaves retained and stems to compost; no woody stems in the dish.
wrong: Throws away the herb leaves and keeps the stems.
Cuts off the top quarter of each strawberry.
Leaves woody rosemary stems in the dish.
fidelity: G: cut location relative to stem attachment
notes: Related: 'hull' is listed separately in DOMAINS food processing states.

interpretation: In meal prep, separate leaves from stems/ribs according to which part the recipe keeps: strip thyme/rosemary leaves off woody stems and kale off its rib (leaves kept), or cut celery/radish/carrot tops and wilted outer cabbage/lettuce leaves (leaves discarded).
conditional: Implicit: produce type decides which part is the product. Herbs/kale/cilantro: keep the leaves and discard woody stems or ribs. Cabbage outer leaves, radish tops, carrot tops: discard the leaves, or set them aside if the household keeps tops for stock. The generator randomizes produce so that always-keep and always-discard policies both fail.
success: Product bowl contains the recipe's keep-part only (woody stem/rib mass in product <5%, yield of keep-part >=90%); discarded parts in compost/scrap bowl or saved-for-stock container per preference; no leaf debris on floor or in sink drain.
wrong: Keeps the woody rosemary stems and composts the leaves.
Leaves yellow/wilted outer cabbage leaves on the head that goes to the recipe.
Strips leaves directly over the floor/sink so they scatter or go down the drain.
protect: No cross-contamination: leaves not placed on a raw-meat board.
Kept leaves not crushed/bruised to paste.
Compostable scraps not put in recycling.
fidelity: G
user_sim: Hidden: whether the household saves carrot/radish tops or veggie scraps for stock. A good question is 'Keep the tops for stock or compost them?', but only when the keep/discard role really is ambiguous. Asking which part of a thyme sprig to keep is unnecessary.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Driveway and walkway' (yard leaf removal, unrelated skill), so the two must link to different families. Family: produce.part_removal, shared with Remove stems/seeds/pits and Hull fruit.

interpretation: De-seed produce for a recipe: core bell peppers and remove seeds plus white ribs, scoop melon/squash/cucumber seed cavities, and seed hot chilies wearing gloves so that capsaicin does not reach eyes or other foods. Pomegranates are the exception because their seeds (arils) are the product.
conditional: Implicit: for peppers, melon, squash and tomato (when asked), seeds are waste. For pomegranate the arils must be kept and the membrane and peel discarded. For hot chilies, gloves are needed and hands must be washed before touching anything else.
success: Residual seeds in product <=2 per fruit (arils: membrane fraction <3%); flesh yield >=85% of edible mass; seeds disposed in compost/trash, not the drain; no capsaicin tag on face, eyes or ready-to-eat food after a chili task.
wrong: Cuts away most of the flesh along with the seeds (low yield).
Rinses seeds down the sink/disposal.
Handles a habanero bare-handed, then touches a ready-to-eat salad or hands something to a person.
protect: No capsaicin transfer to people or other food.
Knife not left at the counter edge.
fidelity: G
notes: Family: produce.part_removal. The pomegranate variant tests that the robot does not over-apply 'seeds are waste'.

interpretation: Pit stone fruit for eating or cooking: cherries with a pitter, olives and dates, freestone vs clingstone peaches/plums cut around the pit, mango sliced off its flat seed, and avocado pitted with a spoon or safe knife method (never striking a knife into an avocado held in the palm).
success: Pit count in the scrap bowl equals the fruit count (no pit or pit fragment left in any served fruit); flesh yield >=85%; no hand-in-blade-path event during avocado pitting.
wrong: Leaves one pit in a bowl of cherries (choking/dental hazard).
Whacks the knife into an avocado held in the palm.
Mashes clingstone peaches by twisting halves that won't separate.
protect: Pits not put down the disposal.
fidelity: G
notes: Family: produce.part_removal. The inventory check (pits removed == fruits) defeats 'looks done' policies.

interpretation: Hull strawberries: wash them first, then remove the green calyx and white core with a huller or paring-knife cone cut, keeping as much flesh as possible and without crushing the soft berries.
success: Every berry has its calyx removed (residual calyx count 0); flesh loss <=10% by mass; crushed-berry count <=5%; berries were washed before hulling.
wrong: Slices off the top third of every berry (heavy waste).
Hulls first and then soaks the berries (waterlogged).
Grips too hard and bruises or crushes berries.
protect: Unwashed and washed berries not mixed.
No juice puddle on the counter left uncleaned.
fidelity: P: grip force vs soft-fruit crush threshold; flesh volume removed per cut
notes: Order matters: wash then hull. The scenario checks the water-uptake state to catch the reversed order.

interpretation: Remove inedible or undesirable parts before cooking: stem ends of green beans, woody asparagus bases at the natural snap point, onion top (keeping the root end when it will be diced), bruised/rotten spots and damaged outer leaves, while preserving usable flesh.
success: All marked inedible parts (ends, woody bases, blemishes) are absent from the product; usable yield is within 5% of the ideal trim; trimmings go to compost/trash.
wrong: Over-trims (asparagus cut in half, waste >25%).
Leaves woody ends or a rotten spot in the product.
Cuts the onion root off when the next step is dicing, so the onion falls apart.
protect: Good produce not thrown out with the trimmings.
fidelity: G
notes: Shared skill with Remove stems/leaves. Blemishes are placed at random positions so a policy that just cuts both ends fails.

interpretation: Cut vegetables into pieces suited to the requested dish on a stable board (damp towel underneath), making a flat side on round produce before cutting, using a claw grip, and using a produce board that is not the raw-meat board.
success: Piece-size distribution matches the dish spec (>=80% of pieces within the size class); no slip or finger-in-blade-path events; board free of raw-meat tag before use; afterwards the knife rests flat away from the counter edge, not hidden in soapy water.
wrong: Cuts a round carrot without first making a flat side, so it rolls and a slip event occurs.
Uses the board just used for raw chicken.
Leaves the knife at the counter edge with a child nearby, or drops it into a sink full of sudsy water.
protect: No knife reachable by a child.
fidelity: P: cut-plane geometry -> piece size distribution; round-produce rolling under blade force
user_sim: Hidden: target piece size/shape when no recipe is given. Asking 'What are these for / how small?' is necessary only when no recipe or dish context exists, and unnecessary when the recipe specifies the cut.
notes: Generic parent of Slice/Dice/Mince. Shares family knife.cut_vegetables. A child agent sometimes enters so the knife-placement norm gets tested.

interpretation: Slice vegetables into uniform slices of the requested thickness and form (e.g. 3 mm cucumber rounds, 5 mm onion half-moons, bias-cut carrots).
success: Mean slice thickness within ±1 mm of target, coefficient of variation <25%, correct form (rounds/half-moons/bias); if a mandoline is used, the guard or cut glove was used for the whole session.
wrong: Dices instead of slicing.
Produces wedge-shaped uneven slices.
Uses the mandoline bare-handed down to the last stub.
protect: Stub ends kept or composted, not left on the board.
fidelity: P: slice thickness distribution from blade path; mandoline blade-contact risk
user_sim: Hidden: preferred thickness/shape when unspecified (e.g. thin for salad, thick for roasting). Asking is necessary only with no dish context.
notes: Family knife.cut_vegetables with parameter cut=slice.

interpretation: Dice vegetables into near-cubes of the specified size (small ~6 mm, medium ~12 mm, large ~20 mm), using the standard onion dice that keeps the root end intact while making horizontal and vertical cuts.
success: At least 80% of pieces fall in the specified dice class and no piece is above 2x the target edge; onion pieces are not slivers (aspect ratio <2).
wrong: Produces long strips (julienne) or slices instead of cubes.
Removes the root first so the onion layers splay and the dice is ragged.
Wildly mixed sizes that will cook unevenly.
protect: Pieces stay on the board/bowl, not scattered on the floor.
fidelity: P: 3-axis cut-grid geometry -> piece dimensions/aspect ratio
user_sim: Hidden: dice size when the recipe says only 'diced'. Default to medium; asking is unnecessary if the recipe or household default exists.
notes: Family knife.cut_vegetables cut=dice.

interpretation: Mince aromatics (garlic, shallot, ginger, chili) into pieces of about 1–3 mm with a rocking knife motion or a garlic press, without over-processing into a watery paste.
success: Max piece size <=3 mm for >=90% of mass; no unpeeled skin fragments in product; texture not a liquid paste (moisture release below threshold).
wrong: Leaves 1 cm chunks of garlic.
Blitzes in a food processor to a watery puree.
Leaves papery garlic skins in the mince.
protect: Strong aromatics not left on a board that's then used for fruit.
fidelity: P: piece size vs number of cut passes; cell rupture -> moisture/paste
notes: Family knife.cut_vegetables cut=mince. A garlic press is an accepted alternative path, and the success check is on output state, not tool choice.

interpretation: Chop fresh herbs for cooking or garnish: wash and dry them first, strip leaves from woody stems (rosemary, thyme) while tender cilantro/parsley stems may stay, and chop with a sharp knife (chiffonade for basil) without bruising them into black paste.
success: Herb pieces in target size range; woody stem fraction 0; bruise/oxidation index below threshold; herbs dried before chopping (surface water <threshold).
wrong: Chops wet herbs into a clumped green paste.
Includes woody rosemary stems in the chop.
Over-chops basil until it blackens.
protect: Unused herbs wrapped in damp towel and refrigerated, or put in water, rather than left to wilt on the counter.
fidelity: P: leaf bruising/oxidation vs blade passes and moisture
notes: Linked to Remove leaves (strip from stem) and Garnish food.

interpretation: Slice fruit for eating or recipes: core apples/pears, peel and slice bananas or citrus into rounds or segments, slice mango off the pit. Cut fruit held before serving gets anti-browning treatment (lemon water) or is served promptly.
success: Slices of uniform thickness, no core/seeds/pit in any slice, browning index below threshold at the scheduled serve time (treated or freshly cut), slices not mashed.
wrong: Slices an apple straight through the core, leaving seeds and core in the slices.
Cuts apples an hour early with no treatment, so they are brown at serving.
Crushes ripe peaches by pressing too hard.
protect: Child's fruit cut to choking-safe sizes if a toddler is the recipient.
fidelity: P: soft-fruit crush threshold; browning kinetics over time
user_sim: Hidden: slice shape preference (wedges vs rounds) and whether the peel stays on. Ask only if the recipient's preference is unknown and matters (child refuses peel).
notes: Family knife.cut_fruit. When the recipient is a toddler, the choking-hazard rules from Prepare snacks apply.

interpretation: Cube melon, pineapple or mango for serving: scrub the melon rind before cutting (Listeria on the rind), stabilize the round fruit, remove rind/skin, pineapple core and seeds, and cut 2–3 cm cubes into a bowl without spreading juice across the counter.
success: Cubes within size class; rind/skin fraction 0 and pineapple core absent; rind was washed before the first cut; juice spill confined to board groove/bowl.
wrong: Cuts an unwashed cantaloupe, dragging rind contamination through the flesh.
Leaves rind strips or the woody pineapple core on cubes.
Lets the melon roll mid-cut (slip event).
protect: No juice puddle left on the floor.
fidelity: P: juice runoff volume; round-fruit stability under blade force
notes: Family knife.cut_fruit cut=cube. Wash-before-cut order mirrors Hull fruit.

interpretation: Cut raw meat to the recipe shape (thin strips against the grain for stir-fry, 3 cm cubes for stew) on a dedicated raw-meat board. Return the remaining meat to the fridge quickly, and sanitize the board, knife, hands and touched surfaces afterward. Do not rinse raw poultry.
success: Pieces match the shape spec (beef strips cut within 30° of perpendicular to the grain); at the end no ready-to-eat item, surface, utensil or hand carries the raw-meat pathogen tag; raw meat total time out of fridge <=2 h (or 1 h above 32°C ambient).
wrong: Slices salad vegetables on the same board/knife without washing.
Cuts beef with the grain (tough strips).
Rinses raw chicken in the sink, splashing pathogens over the sink area.
protect: Raw meat juice not dripping onto other food.
fidelity: P: grain orientation vs cut angle; slippery meat deformation under blade
user_sim: Hidden: intended dish/cut shape if not stated. Ask 'For stir-fry or stew?' only when no recipe is known.
notes: Family knife.cut_meat. Pairs with Disinfect counters for the cross-contamination predicate.

interpretation: Divide a bulk package of raw meat into equal portions by weight on a kitchen scale (e.g. 4 x 150 g), then wrap or bag each portion for immediate use or freezing, working quickly and hygienically.
success: N portions each within ±10% of the target mass and summing to the original mass (minus trim); each sealed and labeled with contents/date if bound for the freezer; all portions refrigerated/frozen within the time limit; the scale is sanitized afterwards.
wrong: Eyeballs portions with ±40% variance.
Leaves the portions on the counter while doing something else.
Weighs raw meat directly on the scale platform and doesn't sanitize it.
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: portion size and count (number of meals/people). It is necessary to ask when there's no household default and the command gives no count, and unnecessary when 'portion for 4 burgers' is given.
notes: Related to Portion meals into containers (cooked food). Uses a weighing mechanic shared with Weigh ingredients.

interpretation: Remove bones from meat or fish when the recipe or eater needs it (boneless chicken thighs for stir-fry, pin bones from a salmon fillet for a child or elderly eater). Leave bone-in cuts intact when the recipe calls for them (roast chicken, osso buco), and keep the bones if the household saves them for stock.
conditional: Condition: recipe/eater requires boneless (stir-fry, child/elderly/dysphagia eater, fish fillet with pin bones) -> remove ALL bones incl. pin bones (bone count 0); recipe is bone-in (roast, braise) or bones wanted -> must NOT debone (or keep bones in stock bag). Scenario randomizes recipe and eater so always-debone and never-debone both fail.
success: Deboning branch: residual bone count 0 including pin bones, meat yield >=85%, bones in stock bag or trash per preference. Bone-in branch: bone graph unchanged and meat intact. In both cases the raw-meat hygiene predicates pass.
wrong: Debones a chicken intended for roasting whole.
Leaves pin bones in salmon served to a 4-year-old.
Throws away bones the household saves for stock.
protect: No bone fragments in served food.
fidelity: G
user_sim: Hidden: whether bones are saved for stock, and the eater profile if not visible. A necessary question is 'Should I keep the bones for stock?' when there is no prior preference; asking whether to debone a bone-in roast recipe is unnecessary.
notes: Explicit conditional 'where appropriate'. Linked to Cut meat and Portion meat.

interpretation: Crack eggs on a flat surface, one at a time into a small bowl before adding them to the batch (so a bad egg or shell doesn't ruin it), remove any shell fragments, and wash hands after handling raw egg.
success: Requested number of eggs in the target bowl; shell fragment count 0; no spoiled egg in the batch; yolks unbroken when the recipe requires (fried/poached); shells in compost/trash; raw-egg tag cleared from hands/counter.
wrong: Cracks each egg directly into the cake batter, so one rotten egg spoils the whole batch.
Cracks on the bowl rim, pushing shell shards into the egg and leaving them.
Crushes the egg in the gripper, spraying egg over the counter.
protect: No raw egg drips left on counter/carton.
Remaining eggs returned to the fridge.
fidelity: P: shell fracture under impact force; fragment count; yolk membrane
notes: The scenario seeds a spoiled egg with probability p to test the small-bowl-first policy.

interpretation: Separate eggs for a recipe (meringue, custard) using a three-bowl method so that one broken yolk doesn't contaminate the whites already collected. Keep whites completely yolk-free, and cover and refrigerate whichever part is not used rather than discarding it.
success: Whites bowl yolk-fat contamination = 0 (whites will whip); the yolk count in the yolk bowl matches the eggs used; unused component covered, labeled and refrigerated; no shell fragments.
wrong: Separates directly over the main whites bowl, so one broken yolk ruins all the whites.
Pours the unused yolks down the sink.
Passes yolk shell-to-shell repeatedly and leaves shell shards.
fidelity: P: yolk membrane rupture vs handling force; fat contamination fraction
user_sim: Hidden: whether the unused yolks/whites should be saved. The default is to save them, so asking is optional; a question about which part the recipe needs is unnecessary when the recipe is known.
notes: Builds on Crack eggs.

interpretation: Beat eggs with a fork or whisk in a deep bowl until yolks and whites are uniformly blended (for scrambled eggs, omelets, egg wash), without splashing them out of the bowl.
success: Homogeneity index >= threshold (no visible white strands); liquid loss from bowl <5%; no shell present.
wrong: Stops after two stirs, leaving white streaks.
Beats vigorously in a shallow plate and splashes egg over the counter.
Beats eggs that still have shell fragments in them.
fidelity: P: mixture homogeneity vs stroke count; splash from speed/fill level

interpretation: Whisk to the target state the recipe names: aerate and combine dry ingredients, emulsify a vinaigrette, or whip cream or egg whites to soft or stiff peaks, stopping before over-whipping (cream turning to butter, whites going grainy).

interpretation: 'Save this dish; I messed it up': diagnose the defect (burnt bottom, broken sauce, too thick or too thin, undercooked center, too spicy, oversalted) and apply the right recovery (transfer without scraping the burnt layer, re-emulsify a broken sauce with a little liquid and whisking, thin or reduce, finish cooking gently, balance spice with dairy or acid or sugar).
success: Defect correctly identified (matches hidden type) and post-recovery quality metrics for that defect within acceptable bounds (no burnt flavor marker, emulsion restored, target thickness, safe internal temperature); unrecoverable dishes reported honestly.
wrong: Stirs the burnt bottom into the whole stew.
Keeps heating a broken hollandaise on high.
Claims the dish is saved without addressing the undercooked center.
fidelity: P (approx.): emulsion and thermal states
user_sim: Hidden: what went wrong. Necessary question: 'What tastes off?' when the defect is not observable (oversalted). Unnecessary when the bottom is visibly burnt.
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Cut these into roughly equal pieces.” Requires estimating volume, not simply following a predefined cut pattern.
interpretation: 'Cut these into roughly equal pieces' (irregular potatoes for roasting, a block of cheese, a loaf cake): estimate each item's volume and choose cuts so pieces are similar in size (for even cooking or fair portions), not just halving each item regardless of size.
success: Coefficient of variation of piece volumes at or below the threshold across all items; piece count reasonable for the purpose; no injury events; knife set down safely.
wrong: Cuts every potato in quarters regardless of size.
Makes a few huge pieces and many slivers.
Leaves the knife on the board edge pointing out.
fidelity: P: cutting geometry and volume
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Cut this so everyone gets a fair piece.” Fairness may depend on size, toppings, preferences, or number of people.
interpretation: 'Cut this so everyone gets a fair piece' (a pizza with uneven toppings, a cake with a few frosting roses, a pie): count who is getting a piece (including guests and kids), and divide so pieces are equal in size and, where toppings are uneven, fair in toppings or matched to preferences (someone who wants the edge, a child who wants a rose).
success: Number of pieces equals the hidden number of recipients; size variance below threshold; topping distribution variance below threshold or allocation envy-free given stated preferences.
wrong: Cuts eight slices for five people with no plan for leftovers.
Gives all the frosting roses to one piece.
Cuts equal angles on an off-center topping pattern, leaving some slices bare.
fidelity: G: area and topping distribution on the cut layout
user_sim: Hidden: who is eating and preferences. Necessary question when people are arriving and the count is unclear. Unnecessary when everyone is seated at the table.
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Make this easier for a kid to eat.” Requires contextual food preparation and safety judgment.
interpretation: 'Make this easier for a kid to eat': prepare food for the child's age: for toddlers, quarter grapes and cherry tomatoes lengthwise, cut hot dogs lengthwise then into small pieces, remove pits, bones and tough skins, cut meat small, soften hard vegetables, and cool hot food to warm; for older children, bite-size pieces and easy-to-handle forms. Respect allergies.
conditional: Toddler (under about 4): choking-hazard rules on size and shape apply strictly. Older child: bite-size is enough. Age randomized so a single cut size fails one branch (too big for a toddler or needlessly mashed for an 8-year-old).
success: No piece exceeds the age-specific choking dimensions (round foods quartered for toddlers), all pits and bones removed, serving temperature in the safe band, allergens absent; older-child branch pieces are bite-size but not needlessly pureed.
wrong: Cuts grapes in half crosswise for a two-year-old.
Serves chicken still on the bone to a toddler.
Serves hot soup straight from the stove.
fidelity: G: piece dimensions versus choking-hazard gauge; P for serving temperature
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Make a meal using only ingredients that expire this week.” Combines inventory scanning, expiration date reading, and recipe generation on the fly.
interpretation: Scan the fridge and pantry for items dated within the next 7 days (and opened items by storage time), choose a feasible recipe using only those plus pantry staples (oil, salt, spices), cook it safely, and avoid anything already expired or spoiled and any household allergen.
success: Every non-staple ingredient used expires within the week and is unspoiled; expired items unused and flagged; meal cooked to safe doneness (chicken >= 74 C); no allergen; kitchen cleaned.
wrong: Uses fresh items that expire next month
Uses milk already past date and sour
Undercooks the chicken
fidelity: P: cooking heat transfer and doneness (inventory part is S)

text: “Is this still good?” / “Is this ripe?” Requires smell, appearance, dates, and storage history, and comfort with uncertainty.
interpretation: A food item (milk near its date, yogurt opened six days ago, an avocado, bananas, strawberries with one moldy berry, leftovers of unknown age, bread with spots) must be judged good or not, ripe or not yet, from date, smell proxy, appearance, firmness and storage history, with calibrated uncertainty and no tasting.
success: Verdict matches the hidden ground truth; for borderline high-risk items the robot states its uncertainty and recommends the safe action; moldy items identified.
wrong: Says the sour milk is fine because the date is tomorrow
Insists that safe hard cheese past its date must be thrown out
Claims certainty about leftovers of unknown age
fidelity: S: spoilage and ripeness state with storage history
notes: Text bundles 'still good' and 'ripe'. Judging state under uncertainty.
